html:
Bislama is the English-based creole of Vanuatu, one of the three official languages beside English and French. It grew in the 19th century among islanders taken to work on plantations in Queensland, Fiji and Samoa; see blackbirding.

Its name comes from bêche-de-mer, the sea cucumbers traders collected. Returning workers brought it home, where it became the common tongue of a country with more than 100 local languages.

The independence constitution of 1980 made it the national language, a choice that bridged the English and French halves of the condominium. It is a close cousin of Tok Pisin in Papua New Guinea and Pijin in the Solomon Islands.
